title: Aim a field rover's solar panel at the sun by its shadow sight
instruction: Point the rover's solar panel straight at the sun lamp.
context: Solar-powered field robots and stations are serviced by aiming their panels at the sun; installers check the aim with a sun sight, a pin standing square on the panel whose shadow shrinks to its foot when the panel faces the sun. The panel turns and tilts on a two-axis friction mount on a rover chocked on its charging pad. Unlike TK-RN34VL (turning mugs about the vertical so their handles point at a visible pin), #236 (setting an arm to a stated angle) #999 (panning a head to follow a target) and TK-AKTDPZ (re-pinning an antenna's downtilt bracket to a marked hole), the target is a light source in 3D, reached by turning and tilting together on a mount that only allows those two rotations, with a shadow as the check.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Parking pad: a 34 x 22 cm mat of artificial turf, 0.5 mm, centred at (36, 2), with four yellow PLA wheel chocks (2.2 x 2.6 cm, 1.6 cm tall) taped to it, one in front of each front tyre and one behind each rear tyre, 2 mm clear of the tyres. Rover: a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M with the Bronco body shell, decals removed, the shell painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 cm long, 12.4 cm wide over its black rubber tyres, 11.7 cm tall, wheelbase 15.5 cm, 0.51 kg with a dummy battery and without the mount (the mount's moving parts and the panel add about 50 g), motor off with the drivetrain engaged; parked on the pad with the point midway between its axles at (36, 2), nose pointing away from the robot and turned 35 degrees to the robot's left. Solar mount (3D-printed PLA, grey) on the rover's rear bed, 10 cm behind the axle midpoint on the rover's centre line: a 2 x 2 cm mast 4.5 cm tall (its top 12.5 cm above the table), a turntable 3.6 cm across turning about the vertical (plus or minus 170 degrees), and a yoke 11.8 cm wide carrying a tilt hinge 3.5 cm above the turntable (tilt -5 to 50 degrees, hard stops). Panel: 2 mm balsa-cored plywood with PLA edges, 10 x 7 x 0.4 cm, painted dark blue, 30 g with the handle, balanced on the hinge through its middle (the 10 cm sides parallel to the hinge), with a white paper sighting disc 6 cm across at its centre, printed with two thin dark rings (0.8 mm lines) round the peg's foot, their inner edges 11.4 mm and 24.8 mm from the peg's centre, a dark grey wooden peg 6 mm across standing 6 cm square to the panel at the disc's centre, and an orange PLA flat aiming handle 4.5 x 2.0 x 0.6 cm sticking out of the middle of the panel's near edge, opposite the side that tilts down. Both joints are friction joints that hold the panel wherever it is left. Start: the panel lies flat, turned 15 degrees to the rover's right. Sun lamp: a warm white LED bulb 2.4 cm across on a black steel post 1.2 cm across (with its 6 cm steel base about 0.8 kg in all), clamped to the table, the bulb's centre at (44.6, 18.7), 42.5 cm above the table (39 cm from the panel, 43 degrees above it); it is the brightest light on the table and is in the top camera's view.
scoring: 0 if at any time the rover (the point midway between its axles) is moved more than 2 cm, turned more than 10 degrees from its parked heading, or tilted more than 10 degrees. Otherwise, at the end, with the rover at rest (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) and the panel still (turning less than 0.05 degrees per control step), both for the last 20 control steps (1 s at 20 Hz), and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and no point along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover or the mount's moving parts): 1.0 if the angle between the panel's normal and the line from the panel's centre to the lamp's centre is at most 8 degrees (on a real panel: the peg's shadow ends inside the inner printed ring); 0.5 if it is at most 20 degrees (the shadow ends inside the outer ring); otherwise 0. The bulb's light (2.9 degrees across from the panel) spreads the shadow's tip over about 3 degrees; judge its middle. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Park the rover on its pad at the marked spot and heading; lay the panel flat and turn it 15 degrees to the rover's right (a mark on the turntable). Check that the lamp is the brightest light on the table.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The rover is one rigid body at the crawler's published size and mass, wheels locked; tyre size, outline and centre of mass are estimates. The two-axis mount is two damped joints (0.3 N m s/rad) with no breakaway torque, so the panel moves more easily than on a real friction mount. The sun is a sphere light 1.9 cm across; the score uses the panel's normal and the lamp's position. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached to the panel near its handle several times and drew back; the panel stayed flat, 47 degrees off the lamp); demo: 1.0
